claim: Staphylococcus aureus clonal complex 8 (CC8) is made up of several subtypes with varying levels of clinical burden, including community-associated methicillin-resistant S. aureus USA300 strains, hospital-associated (HA-MRSA) USA500 strains, and ancestral methicillin-susceptible (MSSA) strains.
source: The Staphylococcus aureus clonal complex 8 (CC8) is made up of several subtypes with varying levels of clinical burden; from community-associated methicillin-resistant S. aureus USA300 strains to hospital-associated (HA-MRSA) USA500 strains and ancestral methicillin-susceptible (MSSA) strains.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract describing the composition of CC8.

claim: Gene-level analysis comparing USA300 against MSSA and HA-MRSA strains have revealed key horizontally acquired genes important for its rapid spread in the community.
source: Gene-level analysis comparing USA300 against MSSA and HA-MRSA strains have revealed key horizontally acquired genes important for its rapid spread in the community.
evidence: This statement references previous findings from gene-level comparative analyses.

claim: Efforts to define the contributions of point mutations and indels have been confounded by strong linkage disequilibrium resulting from clonal propagation.
source: However, efforts to define the contributions of point mutations and indels have been confounded by strong linkage disequilibrium resulting from clonal propagation.
evidence: This describes a limitation in current approaches to studying USA300 mutations.

claim: Independent component analysis on 670 RNA-sequencing samples from USA300 and non-USA300 CC8 strains predicted several genes with strain-specific altered expression patterns.
source: Next, we reconstructed the TRN by using independent component analysis on 670 RNA-sequencing samples from USA300 and non-USA300 CC8 strains which predicted several genes with strain-specific altered expression patterns.
evidence: This describes the computational analysis performed in the study.

claim: The isdH gene has a 38-bp deletion containing a Fur-binding site in USA300 strains.
source: Examination of the regulatory region of one of the genes enriched by both approaches, isdH, revealed a 38-bp deletion containing a Fur-binding site and a conserved single-nucleotide polymorphism which likely led to the altered expression levels in USA300 strains.
evidence: This is a specific finding from the analysis of the isdH regulatory region.

claim: The 38-bp deletion in isdH regulatory region likely led to altered expression levels in USA300 strains.
source: Examination of the regulatory region of one of the genes enriched by both approaches, isdH, revealed a 38-bp deletion containing a Fur-binding site and a conserved single-nucleotide polymorphism which likely led to the altered expression levels in USA300 strains.
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of the deletion and observed expression differences.

claim: USA300 strains carry antibiotic resistance cassettes.
source: For example, USA300 strains carry antibiotic resistance cassettes, Panton–Valentine Leukocidin (PVL) associated with pyogenic skin infections, increased ability to colonize locations outside of the nasopharynx, etc. (Young et al., 2019; Diep et al., 2008; Faden et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: USA300 strains carry Panton–Valentine Leukocidin (PVL) associated with pyogenic skin infections.
source: For example, USA300 strains carry antibiotic resistance cassettes, Panton–Valentine Leukocidin (PVL) associated with pyogenic skin infections, increased ability to colonize locations outside of the nasopharynx, etc. (Young et al., 2019; Diep et al., 2008; Faden et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: USA300 strains have increased ability to colonize locations outside of the nasopharynx.
source: For example, USA300 strains carry antibiotic resistance cassettes, Panton–Valentine Leukocidin (PVL) associated with pyogenic skin infections, increased ability to colonize locations outside of the nasopharynx, etc. (Young et al., 2019; Diep et al., 2008; Faden et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Efforts to discern causal mutations in USA300 strains are hampered by strong population-stratification and genome-wide linkage disequilibrium.
source: As these strains often emerge clonally from closely related 'ancestral strains', efforts to discern causal mutations that lead to their increased clinical burden is hampered by strong population-stratification and genome-wide linkage disequilibrium (Steinig et al., 2019; Challagundla et al., 2018b; Bal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies describing this limitation.

claim: Within clade recombination rates tend to be lower in S. aureus, thus preserving the linkage between mutations.
source: Though recombination at species level is common in S. aureus, within clade recombination rates tend to be lower, thus preserving the linkage between mutations (Challagundla et al., 2018b; Uhlemann et al., 2014; Challagundla et al., 2018a; Everitt et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The CC8 pangenome consisted of 19176 gene clusters with 2291 core genes present in at least ~95% of the genomes analyzed.
source: The CC8 pangenome consisted of 19176 gene clusters with 2291 core genes that were present in at least ~95% of the genomes analyzed.
evidence: This is a direct result from the pangenomic analysis performed in the study.

claim: Among the remainder of the genes in CC8, 931 were categorized as accessory genes and 15,954 were found in less than 5% of the genomes.
source: Among the remainder of the genes, 931 were categorized as accessory genes and 15,954 were found in less than 5% of the genomes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct result from the pangenomic analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The CC8 collection formed a closed pangenome, as adding new genomes did not introduce many new genes.
source: The collection formed a closed pangenome, as adding new genomes did not introduce many new genes (Figure 1A), suggesting that our collection had a good gene-level coverage of the CC8 pangenome.
evidence: This is an inference from the pangenome analysis results shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Most of S. aureus genome sequence comprises of ORFs, for example ~84% of TCH1516 genome is part of an ORF.
source: This is reflective of the fact that most of S. aureus genome sequence comprises of ORFs for example ~84% of TCH1516 genome is part of an ORF.
evidence: This is a specific calculation based on the TCH1516 genome.

claim: 1449 genomes were classified as USA300 and 589 genomes as non-USA300.
source: Combining the genetic markers with phylogenetic grouping led to the classification of 1449 genomes as USA300 and 589 genomes as non-USA300 (Figure 1C, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a direct result from the classification procedure described in the study.

claim: Strains previously identified as 'early USA300' were not part of the USA300 classification.
source: Strains previously identified as 'early USA300' were not part of our USA300 classification (Bowers et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes a specific exclusion from the classification scheme with citation.

claim: DBGWAS found k-mers in 149 components associated with 137 unique TCH1516 genes that were enriched in USA300 strains.
source: In total, we found k-mers in 149 components associated with 137 unique TCH1516 genes that were enriched in this analysis, pointing to a large array of mutations that are unique to the USA300 lineage (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct result from the DBGWAS analysis.

claim: There was strong linkage between the k-mers that were enriched in USA300 strains.
source: There was a strong linkage between the k-mers that were enriched in USA300 strains.
evidence: This is a finding from the linkage disequilibrium analysis.

claim: K-mers that were 1.4 million base pairs away still had r2 over 0.9.
source: Surprisingly, even k-mers that were 1.4 million base pairs away (the maximum distance between two sites in the circular 2.8 million base pairs long S. aureus genome) still had r2 over 0.9 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a specific finding from the linkage disequilibrium analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 61 SNPs within ORFs were enriched in USA300 strains.
source: We identified 61 SNPs within ORFs that were enriched in USA300 strains.
evidence: This is a direct result from the mutation analysis.

claim: Of the 36 enriched ORF mutations, only the Asp75Tyr mutation in the cap5E gene was found in other strains.
source: Of the 36 enriched ORF mutations only the Asp75Tyr mutation in the cap5E gene, which was previously shown to ablate capsule production in USA300 strains, was found in other strains (Figure 3C; Boyle-Vavra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a specific finding from the position-specific entropy analysis with citation to previous work.

claim: The Asp75Tyr mutation in cap5E was previously shown to ablate capsule production in USA300 strains.
source: Of the 36 enriched ORF mutations only the Asp75Tyr mutation in the cap5E gene, which was previously shown to ablate capsule production in USA300 strains, was found in other strains (Figure 3C; Boyle-Vavra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Mutations within ORFs in USA300 strains are likely de novo mutations and are not acquired through horizontal gene transfer.
source: Together, our data suggest that mutations within ORFs in USA300 strains are likely de novo mutations and are not acquired through horizontal gene transfer though many of these mutations have occurred in hotspot regions (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the entropy analysis results.

claim: 291 non-USA300 strains and 379 USA300 samples were used to create a single reconstruction of TRN across CC8 using ICA.
source: After stringent QC/QA and curation, 291 non-USA300 strains (e.g. Newman, NCTC8325) and 379 USA300 (e.g. LAC, TCH1516) samples were used to create a single reconstruction of TRN across CC8 using ICA (Sastry et al., 2019; Sastry et al., 2021; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This describes the dataset used for ICA analysis with citations.

claim: Two iModulons captured a large number of genes with different expression levels in the non-USA300 and USA300 strains.
source: In our reconstruction, two iModulons captured a large number of genes with different expression levels in the non-USA300 and USA300 strains (Figure 4A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct result from the ICA analysis shown in figures.

claim: Most of the genes in the strain-specific iModulons belonged to mobile elements associated with USA300 strains such as ACME, SCCmec, Phi-PVL.
source: Most of the genes in the strain-specific iModulons belonged to mobile elements associated with USA300 strains such as ACME, SCCmec, Phi-PVL, etc.
evidence: This is a finding from the iModulon analysis.

claim: The strain-specific iModulons also contained core genes that are present in both strains, pointing to possible differences in gene regulation.
source: However, the iModulons also contained core genes that are present in both strains, pointing to possible differences in gene regulation (Figure 4B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the iModulon analysis with inference about regulation.

claim: 10 core genes with mutations in the ORF or in the regulatory region were also enriched in the strain-specific iModulon.
source: 10 core genes – including isdH, argR1, and araC family regulator – with mutations in the ORF or in the regulatory region were also enriched in the strain-specific iModulon (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a result from mapping DBGWAS mutations to iModulon genes.

claim: The isdH gene showed distinct strain-specific expression levels and had enriched k-mers mapped to the upstream regulatory region.
source: Of these genes, gene isdH, encoding a heme scavenger molecule showed distinct strain-specific expression levels and had enriched k-mers that are mapped to the upstream regulatory region.
evidence: This is a specific finding from the combined DBGWAS and iModulon analysis.

claim: Comparisons of the isdH regulatory region showed a 38-bp deletion in the 5′ untranslated region containing a transcription factor Fur-binding site.
source: Comparisons showed a 38-bp deletion in the 5′ untranslated region containing a transcription factor Fur-binding site (q-val = 0.033e−4) (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a specific finding from the regulatory region comparison with statistical support.

claim: The 38-bp deletion was detected in all of the 1385 USA300 genomes, but only present in 95 of the 589 non-USA300 genomes.
source: This deletion was detected in all of the 1385 USA300 genomes, but only present in 95 of the 589 non-USA300 genomes.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the genome-wide analysis of the deletion.

claim: Fur is a repressor that blocks expression in presence of iron concentration.
source: As Fur is a repressor that blocks expression in presence of iron concentration, this deletion in the Fur-binding site may be responsible for the general increase in isdH expression observed in USA300 samples (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Fur function.

claim: The deletion in the Fur-binding site may be responsible for the general increase in isdH expression observed in USA300 samples.
source: As Fur is a repressor that blocks expression in presence of iron concentration, this deletion in the Fur-binding site may be responsible for the general increase in isdH expression observed in USA300 samples (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the deletion and observed expression patterns.

claim: A second mutation upstream of the predicted –35 binding site was also enriched in USA300.
source: We also found a second mutation upstream of the predicted –35 binding site that was also enriched in USA300.
evidence: This is a finding from the regulatory region analysis.

claim: The MW2 strain did not have the 38 bp deletion, but contained the exact upstream A->T mutation.
source: Interestingly, while the MW2 strain did not have the 38 bp deletion, it contained the exact upstream A->T mutation.
evidence: This is a specific finding from the sequence comparison.

claim: The Fur-binding motif was detected in the 100-bp upstream region of isdH in all but 21 strains out of 3515 non-CC8 strains.
source: We searched for Fur-binding motif in the 100-bp upstream regions from 3515 non-CC8 strains spanning multiple clonal complexes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1). We detected the binding motif in all but 21 strains.
evidence: This is a result from the motif search analysis.

claim: IsdH is a surface receptor that binds to human hemoglobin, causing it to release the heme.
source: This gene encodes IsdH, a surface receptor that binds to human hemoglobin, causing it to release the heme (Ellis-Guardiola et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: S. aureus prefers heme as its iron source over transferrin-bound iron.
source: Despite having many different pathways for obtaining iron, it has been observed that S. aureus prefers heme as its iron source over transferrin-bound iron (Skaar et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: 2033 S. aureus genomes were downloaded for analysis and six were excluded with genome length of less than 2.5 million base pairs.
source: We downloaded 2033 S. aureus genomes for analysis and excluded six of them with genome length of less than 2.5 million base pairs.
evidence: This describes the initial dataset and filtering criteria.

claim: The phylogenetic tree was reconstructed using 24881 core SNPs.
source: Using the pipeline, the contigs and sequences were aligned to the reference TCH1516 genome NC_010079 and plasmids NC_012417, NC_010063 (Highlander et al., 2007) and 24881 core SNPs at were calculated.
evidence: This describes the method and result of phylogenetic tree reconstruction.

claim: SCCmec cassettes were detected in 1588 genomes of which 1358 were SCCmec IVa positive.
source: We detected SCCmec cassettes in 1588 genomes of which 1358 were SCCmec IVa positive.
evidence: This is a result from the SCCmec detection analysis.

claim: 1431 PVL positive genomes were found using BLASTn search.
source: We also found 1431 PVL positive genomes using BLASTn search with PVL encoding genes from USA300 TCH1516 (USA300HOU_RS07645, USA300HOU_RS07650) as reference (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a result from the PVL detection analysis.

claim: The final ICA model was built with 270 components as input, 148 of which were determined to be robust components.
source: Based on this heuristic, the final model was built with 270 components as input, 148 of which were determined to be robust components.
evidence: This describes the parameters of the final ICA model.

claim: Whole-genome comparisons have enabled rapid characterization of genetic basis for antibiotic resistance, increased virulence, host specificity, and altered metabolic capabilities in S. aureus.
source: In Staphylococcus aureus alone, whole-genome comparisons have enabled rapid characterization of genetic basis for antibiotic resistance, increased virulence, host specificity, and altered metabolic capabilities (Young et al., 2019; Bosi et al., 2016; Choudhary et al., 2018; Correction for Copin, 2019; Krishna et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Genome-wide linkage disequilibrium and strong population structure currently limit the differentiation of causative alleles from genetically linked ones.
source: However, genome-wide linkage disequilibrium and strong population structure currently limit the differentiation of causative alleles from genetically linked ones.
evidence: This describes a known limitation in the field.

claim: Methods like bugwas address issues of linkage disequilibrium for single, recurring phenotypes like antibiotic resistance by calculating lineage level associations.
source: By calculating lineage level associations, methods like bugwas address these issues for single, recurring phenotypes like antibiotic resistance (Earle et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work describing the bugwas method.

claim: Studies of emerging strains often focus on gene-level analysis such as acquisition of mobile genetic elements or loss of gene function as their effect on phenotype is easier to determine than that of point mutations.
source: Due to this limitation, studies of emerging strains often focus on gene-level analysis such as acquisition of mobile genetic elements or loss of gene function as their effect on phenotype is easier to determine than that of point mutations (Thurlow et al., 2012; Boyle-Vavra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: ICA-based reconstruction of the TRN shows both the static gene–regulator interaction and the dynamic activity of these interactions in a sample-specific manner.
source: By factoring the RNA-sequencing data into a series of signals and their activities, the ICA-based reconstruction of the TRN shows both the static gene–regulator interaction and the dynamic activity of these interactions in a sample-specific manner (Sastry et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing the ICA method.

claim: ICA outputs signals associated with strain-specific changes in gene regulation in addition to signals associated with gene regulators.
source: Therefore, in addition to signals associated with gene regulators, ICA also outputs signals associated with strain-specific changes in gene regulation.
evidence: This describes a property of the ICA method when applied to multi-strain data.

claim: In E. coli and S. enterica Typhimurium, multi-strain ICA has been used to calculate strain-specific iModulons that represent differences in gene expression.
source: In Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica Typhimurium, multi-strain ICA has been used to calculate strain-specific iModulons that represent differences in gene expression (Sastry et al., 2019; Yuan et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous applications of the method.

claim: The transcriptomic analysis consisted of samples primarily from the USA300 (CC8e and CC8f) clades, the CC8a clade represented by Newman and the CC8b clade represented by NCTC8325 and its derivatives.
source: The transcriptomic analysis consisted of samples primarily from the USA300 (CC8e and CC8f) clades, the CC8a clade represented by Newman and the CC8b clade represented by NCTC8325 and its derivatives.
evidence: This describes the composition of the RNA-seq dataset.

claim: The CC8b and CC8a clades are currently undersampled due to their minimal clinical burden compared to USA300.
source: However, the CC8b and CC8a clades are currently undersampled due to its minimal clinical burden compared to USA300.
evidence: This describes a limitation in the available data.

claim: The misalignment of RNA-sequencing samples from GWAS samples may explain the low number of hits that were enriched by both methods.
source: The misalignment of RNA-sequencing samples from GWAS samples may explain the low number of hits that were enriched by both methods when many other unique gene expression patterns have been observed in USA300 strains.
evidence: This is an inference about a limitation of the approach.

claim: Resolving the confounding effect of linkage disequilibrium inherent in emerging and clonal strains will require a new generation of modeling methods.
source: On the other hand, resolving the confounding effect of linkage disequilibrium inherent in emerging and clonal strains will require a new generation of modeling methods (Bal et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a statement about future needs with a citation.

claim: A metabolic allele classifier combining genome scale metabolic models with machine learning was used to estimate biochemical effects of alleles in M. tuberculosis.
source: Our recent work with Mycobacterium tuberculosis utilized a metabolic allele classifier which combines genome scale metabolic models with machine learning to estimate biochemical effects of alleles thus mapping mutations to changes in metabolic fluxes (Kavvas et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Advances in protein structure prediction with AlphaFold2 and RosettaFold enable predicting the effects of mutations on protein folding.
source: Similarly, advances in protein structure prediction with AlphaFold2 and RosettaFold puts us at the cusp of predicting the effects of mutations on protein folding (Baek et al., 2021; Jumper et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent advances in protein structure prediction.

claim: Combination of modeling techniques may prove to be the breakthrough required to advance solutions to current challenges in population genetics of emerging pathogens.
source: Combination of these modeling techniques may therefore prove to be the breakthrough required to advance solutions to the current challenges in population genetics of emerging pathogens.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future directions.

claim: The transcription start site in the isdH regulatory region has been experimentally confirmed in the MW2 strain.
source: Additionally, we included MW2 (CC1 CA-MRSA) as the transcription start site in the region has been experimentally confirmed in this strain (Prados et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to experimental work.

claim: All other base pairs in the isdH regulatory region were perfectly matched between all the reference genomes except for the identified mutations.
source: All other base pairs in the region were perfectly matched in between all the reference genomes.
evidence: This is a finding from the sequence comparison.

claim: The combination of evidence from genetic and transcriptomic analysis suggests that regulation of isdH is altered in USA300 strains compared to its non-USA300 progenitors.
source: The combination of evidence from genetic and transcriptomic analysis suggests that regulation of isdH is altered in USA300 strains compared to its non-USA300 progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence from the study.

claim: The absence of Fur-binding site upstream of isdH gene is prevalent only in the USA300 lineage among CC8 strains.
source: As with many point mutations detected in our analysis, the absence of Fur-binding site upstream of isdH gene is prevalent only in the USA300 lineage.
evidence: This is a finding from the genome-wide analysis of the deletion.

claim: Of the 21 non-CC8 strains with no detectable Fur-binding sites upstream of isdH, 6 belonged to ST72 out of 28 total from this type.
source: Of the 21 strains with no detectable Fur-binding sites, 6 belonged to ST72 (out of 28 total from this type) and 6 had uncharacterized multilocus sequence type (MLST).
evidence: This is a result from the motif search analysis across non-CC8 strains.

claim: IsdH is part of an arsenal of S. aureus iron sequestration proteins including Staphyloferrins and ferrous iron transporters.
source: It is part of an arsenal of S. aureus iron sequestration proteins including Staphyloferrins and ferrous iron transporters that it uses to compete with the host for essential iron (van Dijk et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: USA300 strains with the deleted Fur-binding site showed general increase in isdH expression level.
source: In congruence with this observation, we also found that USA300 strains with the deleted Fur-binding site showed general increase in isdH expression level.
evidence: This is a finding from the expression analysis.

claim: Combining GWAS with large-scale transcriptomic modeling was able to predict potential causal mutations contributing to the increased clinical burden of the USA300 lineage.
source: Combining GWAS with large-scale transcriptomic modeling was therefore able to predict potential causal mutations contributing to the increased clinical burden of the USA300 lineage.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the utility of the combined approach.

claim: The current analysis utilized available DNA- and RNA-sequencing data and the methods used are scalable to the rapidly growing number of data in public repositories.
source: The current analysis utilized the available DNA- and RNA-sequencing data and the methods used here are scalable to the rapidly growing number of data in the public repositories.
evidence: This describes a property of the methods used.

claim: With greater scale, more granular insight into subclade-specific differences can be obtained.
source: Indeed, with the greater scale, we can get more granular insight into subclade-specific differences.
evidence: This is a statement about future potential with more data.

claim: For 28 of the USA300-enriched mutations, a peak in entropy was present in sequences from other clades within 71 MSA positions.
source: Despite not having any perfect matches outside of the cap5E mutation, we found that for 28 of the mutations, a peak was present in sequences from other clades within 71 MSA positions.
evidence: This is a finding from the position-specific entropy analysis.

claim: Many USA300 ORF mutations have occurred in hotspot regions despite being de novo mutations.
source: Together, our data suggest that mutations within ORFs in USA300 strains are likely de novo mutations and are not acquired through horizontal gene transfer though many of these mutations have occurred in hotspot regions (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the entropy analysis results.

claim: DBGWAS recovered components associated with previously described markers of USA300 strains including mecA (SCCmec IVa), arcA (ACME), cap5e mutation, seq, sek, and Phi-PVL.
source: De Bruijn graph genome-wide association study (DBGWAS) recovers components associated with USA300 previously described markers of USA300 strains including mecA (SCCmec IVa), arcA (ACME), cap5e mutation, seq, sek, and Phi-PVL.
evidence: This is shown in Figure 2A and describes validation of the DBGWAS approach.

claim: The USA300 root was placed at the last node where >90% of the strains within the subclade represented by the daughter nodes were SCCmec IVa and PVL positive.
source: The root was placed at the last node where >90% of the strains within the subclade represented by the daughter nodes were SCCmec IVa and PVL positive (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the criterion used for placing the USA300 root.

claim: Root finding with the phylogenetic tree traversal procedure is not dependent on the starting USA300 strain.
source: As phylogenetic trees are nested, root finding with this procedure is not dependent on the starting USA300 strain.
evidence: This is a property of the method used.

claim: The same USA300 root was identified when the procedure was initialized with FPR3757 instead of TCH1516.
source: Same root was identified when the procedure was initialized with another well-known USA300 reference strain FPR3757 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This validates the robustness of the root-finding procedure.

claim: A larger number of mutations were found within the ORFs than in the neighboring regulatory regions.
source: We found a larger number of mutations within the ORFs, indicating the presence of greater genetic variation in the ORFs than in the neighboring regulatory regions.
evidence: This is a finding from the mutation survey.

claim: Each PATRIC protein family comprised 2000–16,000 unique sequences spanning dozens of clades.
source: After filtering, each protein family comprised 2000–16,000 unique sequences and the strains from which the amino acid sequences were derived spanned dozens of clades allowing for broad comparisons (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the dataset used for the entropy analysis.

claim: ST239 sequences were removed from the analysis as it is thought to have emerged from large-scale recombination of ST8 and ST30 strains.
source: Lastly, we removed sequences associated with ST239 as it is thought to have emerged from large-scale recombination of ST8 and ST30 strains (Robinson and Enright, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and describes a filtering step.

claim: Allelic entropy at a given amino acid position is a function of the number of unique amino acids found in that position and the frequency of the mutation.
source: Allelic entropy at a given amino acid position is a function of the number of unique amino acids found in that position and the frequency of the mutation (Hyun et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation describing the method.

claim: Positions where all queried sequences have the same amino acid have low entropy, while positions that have frequent amino acid substitutions have high entropy.
source: Positions where all queried sequences have the same amino acid have low entropy, while positions that have frequent amino acid substitutions (hotspots) have high entropy (Figure 3B).
evidence: This describes the interpretation of the entropy measure.
